meta.note: Correlation register. The brief asks us to determine correlation values. No league-official, government-official or regulator-official source publishes a player-prop correlation matrix, and no historical joint-outcome data has been ingested. Therefore every Magnitude cell on this page is EMPTY and flagged. The Direction column states a structural expectation about how football works, which is reasoning about the game, not a measurement of data.
meta.blank_cell_rule: An empty magnitude cell means we do not know the number. It is never filled with a plausible-looking value.
estimation_plan: 1. Define the pair universe and freeze it.
2. Collect historical joint outcomes for every pair over a fixed window.
3. Estimate the phi coefficient on the binary over/under outcomes, and the Pearson or Spearman coefficient on the continuous underlying statistics.
4. Hold out a later window and check that the estimated correlation predicts joint hit rates out of sample.
5. Only then allow the pair into parlay or prop-combo pricing.
6. Re-estimate every season; publish the version and the window with each value.

algebra.name: Parlay price under independence
algebra.formula: P(all legs win) = P(leg 1) x P(leg 2) x ... x P(leg n)
algebra.note: This is the naive model. It is correct only if the legs are independent, and football props almost never are.

algebra.name: Joint probability with a known phi coefficient
algebra.formula: P(A and B) = P(A)P(B) + rho * sqrt( P(A)(1-P(A)) * P(B)(1-P(B)) )
algebra.note: This is the definition of the phi coefficient rearranged. It is algebra, not an estimate - but it needs rho, and rho is exactly what we do not have.

algebra.name: Error from assuming independence
algebra.formula: pricing error = rho * sqrt( P(A)(1-P(A)) * P(B)(1-P(B)) )
algebra.note: This is the size of the mistake made by naively multiplying. With a moderate positive rho and two legs near even money, the error is material relative to a typical margin. The direction of the harm depends on the sign of rho: positive correlation makes a parlay more likely to win than naive multiplication says, negative correlation makes it less likely.

algebra.name: Worked illustration with deliberately synthetic inputs
algebra.formula: Take P(A) = P(B) = 0.50 and a hypothetical rho = 0.30. Naive independence gives P = 0.25. Applying ALG-2 gives P = 0.25 + 0.30 * sqrt(0.25 * 0.25) = 0.25 + 0.075 = 0.325.
algebra.note: The 0.50 and 0.30 values are invented solely to demonstrate the arithmetic. They are NOT measurements, NOT estimates from data, and must never be used in pricing. They are shown here because the formula is easier to audit with numbers in it.

pairs.why: Both legs are driven by the same passing volume. If the quarterback throws for more, his receiver almost necessarily gains more.
pairs.estimation: Phi coefficient on the binary prop outcomes; Pearson on the season-level underlying statistics.

pairs.why: Game script. A team that is leading runs the ball; a team that is trailing throws. Passing volume and rushing volume on the same team are partly substitutes.
pairs.estimation: Phi coefficient, stratified by the closing spread so that script-driven correlation is separated from team style.

pairs.why: Total points and passing yards are both increasing in the number of plays and in offensive success.
pairs.estimation: Phi coefficient; also Pearson on the continuous residuals after regressing out the pre-game total.

pairs.why: A team that is winning runs the ball to close the game out, so covering and rushing volume move together.
pairs.estimation: Phi coefficient conditional on the closing spread bucket, because the strength of the script effect depends on how big the spread is.

pairs.why: A passing touchdown is almost always also a receiving touchdown for someone on that team.
pairs.estimation: Phi coefficient. Note that this pair is frequently restricted or refused by operators for exactly this reason.

pairs.why: Both are increasing in attempts and completion rate. This is close to a mechanical relationship, so the correlation should be high.
pairs.estimation: Pearson on the underlying statistics; expect the highest value in this register.

pairs.why: More catches usually means more yards, but the relationship is weaker than it looks because yards per catch varies enormously.
pairs.estimation: Pearson on the underlying statistics; report the conditional version given the player's season yards-per-catch.

pairs.leg_b: Player B anytime touchdown, same team
pairs.why: Touchdowns within a team are partly cannibalised: a score by one player is a scoring opportunity not taken by another, particularly in the red zone.
pairs.estimation: Phi coefficient, restricted to players who share a position group.

pairs.why: A scoring player contributes directly to his team's point total.
The two outcomes are mutually exclusive and exhaustive apart from a tie. This is the one pair in this register whose value is known by definition rather than by measurement.
Games in which the favourite runs away with it tend to be higher scoring than the market implied.
pairs.estimation: Phi coefficient, stratified by total bucket.

pairs.why: Volume is the dominant driver of rushing yards.

pairs.leg_a: Team A QB passing yards over
pairs.leg_b: Team B QB passing yards over
pairs.why: Shootout script: when one team is throwing heavily, the other is often forced to as well.
pairs.estimation: Phi coefficient conditional on the pre-game total, which already prices much of this.

pairs.why: Nearly the same event counted from two sides. Operators commonly refuse this combination.
pairs.estimation: Phi coefficient. Expect near-perfect positive correlation where the markets align.

pairs.why: Scoring in the first half contributes to the full-game total.
pairs.estimation: Pearson on the underlying point totals.

pairs.why: Drives that stall in field-goal range produce both a made field goal and fewer points than a touchdown drive would have.
pairs.estimation: Phi coefficient; also test the red-zone efficiency signal (SIG-010) here.

pairs.why: A defensive score adds points but usually shortens the game and reflects defensive pressure. The net effect is not obvious from reasoning alone, which is precisely why it must be measured rather than guessed.
pairs.estimation: Phi coefficient with an explicit power check; if the sample is too small, leave the cell blank permanently rather than reporting a noisy number.

pairs.leg_b: Team A player prop, same team
pairs.why: Team success and individual production on that team move together.
pairs.estimation: Phi coefficient, reported per position group because the strength differs materially by position.

guardrails: No pair enters parlay or prop-combo pricing until its magnitude has been estimated and checked out of sample.
A pair whose correlation is unknown is treated as unknown, not as zero. Assuming zero is itself an assumption and it is the one that misprices parlays.
Every published magnitude carries its estimation window, sample size and version. A number without those is not a result.
Where operators refuse a combination outright, record that as a market-structure fact rather than trying to price around it.
